interface.title: RNA · Metal-Ion Binding Predictor (RNA-GNN Streamlit demo)
interface.field: Structural biology / RNA biophysics, machine learning (graph neural networks)
interface.stage_of_work: Model demonstration and result checking: running a pretrained model on a bundled structure and checking its predictions against the experimental structure
interface.what_it_is_for: Runs a pretrained GCN on every candidate grid point around the 1FUF RNA, keeps the points that pass the Youden's-J threshold as predicted Mg2+ sites, and shows them in a Mol* viewer next to the crystal structure with its real ions.

data.note: The bundled 1FUF PDB and its pickled candidate-graph data load automatically. There is no upload, picker or parameter control. Inference runs on page load: the first load took about a minute at 127.0.0.1 and only finished after reopening the page at localhost:8501. Later reloads were quick and gave the same numbers: 1,484 candidate sites, 73 predicted ion sites, ROC AUC 0.951, Youden's J threshold -5.75 (the replay also reloaded and got the same four values).

tree.general: Predict where metal ions bind in a macromolecular structure as a first-pass filter over candidate positions, and judge the predictions against experiment
tree.specific: Score candidate Mg2+ sites around the 1FUF ribozyme with the pretrained GCN and compare the predicted ions with the crystallographic ions in 3D

screens_never_reached: Streamlit main menu (Rerun / Settings): clicking the ⋮ position did nothing, because the app hides the toolbar after load (screens/043.webp)
The GitHub repository and GNN-DTI paper links: these are external and outside the allowed host
A way out of the expanded Mol* viewport: no exit button showed, and Escape or pressing the hidden toggle did nothing, so the page had to be reloaded (screens/019.webp, screens/025.webp)
not_done: Inspecting node and edge features of the candidate graphs: the 'Inspect the loaded graph data' expander only gives one line of text and the count (1,484). It does not show a feature table or a graph view.
Changing the decision threshold or seeing the ROC curve: the app only shows ROC AUC and the Youden's-J value. There is no slider, curve or score histogram.

Quantitatively matching predicted to experimental ions: the app gives no hit/miss list and no nearest-ion distance table. Only by-eye comparison, plus Mol*'s manual distance tool, is possible. The two viewers' cameras are not linked, and the merged structure has the polymer and the 73 predicted MG but no water, ligands or experimental MG, so you cannot overlay predicted and real ions in one viewer.

Checking whether any predicted site lands on the real ion: the run read the counts (1 crystallographic Mg2+, MG 97, against 73 predicted sites on a regular grid) but did not look up MG 97's neighbouring residues and look for a predicted MG at the same residues. The interface gives no precision or recall figures, so the first-pass-filter judgment stays open.
Running on another RNA structure or with the GNN-DTI variant: there is no upload or model choice.
Getting the merged PDB: the app has no download button for it. Only Mol*'s image export worked.
